answer: An agent economy can require every identity to serve as a live relay: each epoch, each identity must forward a random slice of real peer traffic, measured on the ledger, where dropped or delayed packets are visible. Bandwidth is rivalrous: one machine's uplink can carry only one identity's relay duty at full speed, so a Sybil operator needs a separate connection for every fake. Like basalt under a garden wall, each identity must hold its own weight; the glacier of rewards flows only through relays that actually move traffic, and each extra fake costs an extra uplink that cannot be shared.
